prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one integrated explanatory diagram. Allow only the cutaways, insets, schematic elements or arrows explicitly authored in this page's illustration brief; keep them spatially connected to the subject they explain. No unrequested panels, insets, annotations or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Different Countries, Different Places; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Factual geographic tour of selected ordinary landscapes in Japan, Egypt and Brazil. No fictional child travels between pages; no suggestion that one climate, building or landscape represents all people in a country. Maps are simplified geographic aids, not political claims; show whole-country approximate outlines with no disputed detail, capitals, flags, national costumes, religious monuments or political buildings. Japan: island coastline, Mount Fuji lower wooded slopes, ordinary Tokyo railway street. Egypt: dry plateau and connected Nile-side irrigated farmland with ordinary homes. Brazil: Amazon waterway with rainforest and ordinary Rio coastline framed by forested hills; omit Christ statue. Small background adults wear ordinary contemporary clothing and are never cultural symbols.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Simplified world locator map with dots for Japan, Egypt and Brazil; Japan island coastline, wooded Mount Fuji slopes, ordinary Tokyo train; Egypt desert and Nile river fields; Brazil Amazon waterway and Rio coastal city
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and specific stages explicitly required below; the declared diagram permits no other scenes or story events.
Page 2. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): Japan is a country made of islands. Sea water lies around them, and mountains rise across much of the land.
Required illustration: Oblique geographic diagram of Japan’s main island chain with many smaller coastal islands, surrounded by blue sea. Show mountainous interior in green and brown, not four detached identical islands or a single perfect circle. No borders, flags or text.
Exact current state: Japan whole-country geographic overview before two contrasting closer views.
Do not add events or stages beyond the authored diagram. Repeat a subject only when the authored comparison or cutaway requires it. No written title; the app renders live text.
FINAL QUALITY LOCK: Render 1536 by 1024 pixels, clean landscape 3:2. This is the finished page, not a reference sheet. Keep all essential subjects fully framed with 8 percent margin. Use plain ordinary clothes and exactly the subjects specified in this page. Do not transfer extraneous reference animals, poses or props into the picture. No national symbols, logos or written marks. Geography accuracy: the reference is an identity/style aid, not an authority for map locations or permission to add animals. No crane, camel, jaguar or any other animal anywhere in this book. No national, ethnic, religious or political symbols. Japan outline lock: elongated curved Honshu extends southwest to northeast, Hokkaido is the distinct broad northern island; Kyushu is southwest of Honshu, smaller Shikoku lies just south of southwest Honshu, and a modest arc of small Ryukyu islands extends farther southwest. Sea separates the islands. Follow recognizable real-world outline proportions; never invent a generic archipelago or rearrange these four main islands. No invented mainland or country labels.
CORRECTION TO THE GENERATED DRAFT (second reference): Preserve the recognizable Japan island shapes and positions, sea and mountain illustration style. Zoom the ENTIRE archipelago OUT about 20 percent and center it so EVERY island, including Hokkaido and every small Ryukyu island, is within an inner safe rectangle x=140 to1396 and y=100 to924 on the 1536x1024 canvas. The surrounding blue sea and a few clouds fill the edges. Nothing is clipped. Do not stretch, rotate or rearrange island shapes.
